quiz_item.question: Your patrol is hiking across an open alpine ridgeline when towering cumulonimbus clouds build rapidly and you hear thunder 10 seconds after seeing a lightning flash (roughly 2 miles away). What is the safest immediate action for the patrol?
options: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.
D. Lie flat on wet granite at the summit so the wind blows over the patrol.
choices: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.

quiz_item.correct_answer: B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.

D. Wait until you see hail larger than golf balls before checking your family or troop emergency shelter plan.

At least two sources of weather Principle 2: It was highly successful at giving meteorologists their first overall view of entire storm systems (p. 33).
At least two sources of weather Principle 3: Since then, satellites have become much more sophisticated, allowing a nearly continuous watch over the entire Earth (p. 33).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (At least two sources of weather): The satellite systems are named Polar Operational Environmental Satellites (POES) and Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (p. 33).
Step 2 (At least two sources of weather): The polar-orbiting satellites circle Earth, passing over or near the poles at a height of approximately 520 miles (p. 33).
Step 3 (At least two sources of weather): They travel around the globe several times each day (p. 33).
Step 4 (At least two sources of weather): The polar-orbiting satellites are placed in sun-synchronous orbits, which means they pass over the same spot at the same time each day (p. 33).

Step 3 (Tilt of Earth's Axis Helps): At the summer solstice (the first day of summer, bottom left), the North Pole tilts toward the sun, and the sun reaches its northernmost point (p. 66).
Step 4 (Tilt of Earth's Axis Helps): This is the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere (p. 66).

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.
D. Lie flat on wet granite at the summit so the wind blows over the patrol.
choices: A. Stay on the ridgeline under a tall isolated pine tree to keep dry until the rain passes.

B. Apply the 30/30 lightning rule: immediately descend off the exposed ridge and away from tall isolated trees or water, move into lower dense timber or a substantial building, and spread patrol members at least 50 feet apart if caught in the open.
C. Huddle together in a tight circle on top of metal-frame backpacks.

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Sound travels about 1 mile every 5 seconds; a 10-second flash-to-bang interval means lightning is within 2 miles and already in strike range, requiring immediate descent from ridges and avoidance of tall isolated objects.

B. A Watch means atmospheric conditions favor severe thunderstorm and tornado development (stay alert and prepared); a Warning means hazardous weather or a tornado is imminent or occurring on radar/ground (take immediate shelter now).
C. Both Watch and Warning mean the storm has already passed your campsite and outdoor activities can resume.
D. Wait until you see hail larger than golf balls before checking your family or troop emergency shelter plan.

C. Both Watch and Warning mean the storm has already passed your campsite and outdoor activities can resume.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Looking at a surface weather map (Requirement 4), your patrol sees a blue line with triangles pointing southeast advancing toward a warm, humid air mass. What frontal system is approaching and what weather should the troop expect?
options: A. A warm front that brings several days of calm, cloudless skies and rising barometric pressure.

B. An advancing cold front where dense cold air wedges abruptly under warm moist air, forcing rapid vertical uplift, towering cumulonimbus clouds, gusty winds, and potential squall-line thunderstorms.
C. A high-pressure ridge where sinking air creates heavy blizzards and stationary fog.
D. A stationary pressure trough where wind stops completely and humidity drops to zero.
choices: A. A warm front that brings several days of calm, cloudless skies and rising barometric pressure.

B. An advancing cold front where dense cold air wedges abruptly under warm moist air, forcing rapid vertical uplift, towering cumulonimbus clouds, gusty winds, and potential squall-line thunderstorms.
C. A high-pressure ridge where sinking air creates heavy blizzards and stationary fog.
D. A stationary pressure trough where wind stops completely and humidity drops to zero.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. An advancing cold front where dense cold air wedges abruptly under warm moist air, forcing rapid vertical uplift, towering cumulonimbus clouds, gusty winds, and potential squall-line thunderstorms.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Cold fronts (blue triangles) push dense cold air beneath lighter warm air, causing steep vertical lifting, rapid cumulus/cumulonimbus buildup, and sudden showers or thunderstorms followed by cooler, drier air (p. 29).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: During a summer afternoon thunderstorm (Requirement 5), your patrol observes jagged lightning bolts and half-inch hailstones. What physical mechanism inside a cumulonimbus cloud produces both hail and lightning?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: During a summer afternoon thunderstorm (Requirement 5), your patrol observes jagged lightning bolts and half-inch hailstones. What physical mechanism inside a cumulonimbus cloud produces both hail and lightning?
options: A. Gentle horizontal breezes blowing across flat stratus clouds below 2,000 feet.

B. Powerful vertical updrafts and downdrafts cycling water droplets above and below the freezing level (accreting layered ice for hail) while colliding ice crystals and graupel separate electrical charges that discharge as lightning.
C. Direct solar radiation melting high-altitude cirrus clouds without any vertical air motion.
D. Ocean tides pulling warm air downward into a high-pressure center.
choices: A. Gentle horizontal breezes blowing across flat stratus clouds below 2,000 feet.

B. Powerful vertical updrafts and downdrafts cycling water droplets above and below the freezing level (accreting layered ice for hail) while colliding ice crystals and graupel separate electrical charges that discharge as lightning.
C. Direct solar radiation melting high-altitude cirrus clouds without any vertical air motion.
D. Ocean tides pulling warm air downward into a high-pressure center.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Powerful vertical updrafts and downdrafts cycling water droplets above and below the freezing level (accreting layered ice for hail) while colliding ice crystals and graupel separate electrical charges that discharge as lightning.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Strong updrafts in cumulonimbus clouds suspend and cycle freezing droplets into layered hailstones while collisions between ice crystals and soft hail (graupel) build high-voltage charge separation that arcs as lightning (p. 34).
